items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: We became real, real close friends.

ctx.x: Well, as far back as I can remember, when I was a little kid, when this particular group of boys would parade on the streets, I'd break my neck to go over there and listen to them. And sometimes they came right down to San Antonio Street, which was about, well, in between the two blocks that I lived. I lived on Robinson and the parade would come down San Antonio Street. I don't know, I don't know, they had a hymn there. How did that happen? What were they doing? Well, just parading, I imagine. I can't recall…

And was that for a school or something? How did that happen? Yes, it was for Jones. Oh, for Jones. That's right. A wave song. A wave song. I see. Well, now, did you get to know him down here? Did you meet him later?
No, I met a lawyer in later years after I had gotten my band and we met, and through other musicians I met there. We became real, real close friends.
